SE.name: Sweden
SE.receiptObligation: Verified (skatteverket.se): every business that takes cash or card payments (incl. Swish) must register sales in a kassaregister and, for every sale, produce and OFFER the customer a kassakvitto, on paper or digitally, regardless of payment method. A card-terminal slip alone is not a kassakvitto. Returns need a returkvitto. Exemptions (verified): sales (cash+card) <= 4 price base amounts incl. VAT per 12-month year (SEK 236,800 for 2026); income-tax-exempt bodies, taxi, distance/home sales, unattended/vending/automated stores, licensed lottery/betting agents, public-transport ticket sales, bingo/gaming; invoiced sales (cash invoice instead); individual exemption by application. Legal basis: Skatteforfarandelagen (2011:1244) ch. 39 (section numbers unverified).
SE.digitalReceipt: Verified: Skatteverket position (4 Dec 2024, dnr 8-3188477) says no requirement for a paper receipt; the merchant may offer paper, electronic, or both; form requirements are technology-neutral. Older commentary: an electronic receipt must be sent from the cash register itself (not just shown on screen). No customer opt-in condition found in Skatteverket sources (unverified whether any consent rule exists beyond GDPR). The register must still be able to print per SKVFS 2009:1 24 par. (a sale cannot be registered unless a receipt is produced at the same time) - how this interacts with digital-only receipts: unverified, confirm with adviser/register supplier.
SE.mandatoryFields: Verified (SKVFS 2009:1 28 par., still the consolidated text referenced by Skatteverket; SKVFS 2014:9 is the current register regulation - exact current wording to be confirmed): company name; organisation number (or personal ID number); address where the sale takes place; date and time; receipt number from an unbroken ascending series; register designation (kassabeteckning); names and quantities of goods / number of services; sales amount; VAT amount; VAT split per rate; payment method(s); control unit's serial/manufacturing number (kontrollenhetens tillverkningsnummer). VAT items not required if the seller's sale is not VAT-liable. Amounts in SEK. Returkvitto has same requirements. Copies must be marked 'KOPI' (at least twice the size of the amount text), max one copy per receipt.
SE.fiscalSystem: Verified: certified-system model. Kassaregister (manufacturer-declared, tillverkardeklaration) must be connected to a certified kontrollenhet (control unit/control system; SKVFS 2009:2, SKVFS 2014:8 for control systems). The control unit receives receipt data from the register and generates a unique kontrollkod per receipt; the register may not register sales unless the control unit is working. Applies to ALL merchants taking cash/card payments unless exempt (see receiptObligation). Registration: the business must notify Skatteverket of the register (and each registration unit). Changes: from 1 Oct 2025 (verified) ID plates on registration units/control units are no longer required, and customers' own registration units (e.g. phones) need not be reported if an equivalent unit with the same control unit/system/program is already reported. From 1 Jan 2027 (verified, skatteverket.se) registers must meet SKVFS 2021:17; registers with journalminne must be able to produce XML records. March 2026: Skatteverket proposed a broad government review of the cash register rules (proposal only, not law).
SE.realTimeReporting: None found. Sweden has no real-time transmission of sales data to Skatteverket; control unit stores data and Skatteverket audits on site / on request (unverified whether any periodic reporting exists: none found).
SE.receiptIdentifiers: Sequential receipt number (unbroken ascending series), register designation, control unit serial number (verified in 28 par.). Control code (kontrollkod) is generated per receipt by the control unit; whether it must be PRINTED on the customer receipt and any QR format: unverified in sources reached (SKVFS 2014:9 PDF could not be parsed). No QR requirement found.
SE.retentionYears: 7 years from end of the calendar year in which the fiscal year ended (Bokforingslagen 7 kap 2 par.) - from general knowledge, NOT verified in this session; register journal/control data follows the same bookkeeping retention. Electronic storage allowed.

vat.reduced: 12% restaurant and catering services (verified via secondary sources citing Skatteverket), hotels/accommodation 12%; food 6% from 1 Apr 2026 to 31 Dec 2027 (temporary, reverts to 12% on 1 Jan 2028; secondary sources); 6% books/newspapers/passenger transport/culture; 0%/exempt categories exist. Eat-in restaurant 12% vs takeaway food 6% in the same business (secondary sources).

other.cashRounding: Cash totals are rounded to whole kronor (ore removed 2010) - from general knowledge, unverified in sources; card payments exact. Rounding line should appear on receipt (unverified).
other.language: Not found; Swedish is normal practice. unverified.

DK.name: Denmark
DK.receiptObligation: Verified (info.skat.dk A.B.3.3.1.6): retailers selling mainly/only to private consumers may choose between issuing simplified invoices or using a sales registration system and giving a till receipt (kassebon). A full invoice is required on request of a business buyer, BoligJob services, private-person services >= DKK 5,000 incl. VAT, and certain EU distance sales. Where a receipt/simplified invoice is not technically possible, a simplified invoice must be issued for sales above DKK 1,000 incl. VAT. Whether a consumer can refuse a receipt: unverified.
DK.digitalReceipt: Verified (skat.dk): in the digital sales registration (digital salgsregistrering) regime, receipts may be sent electronically to a system the customer has accepted IN ADVANCE; a printer is required only if the merchant cannot send electronically to such a system. So customer pre-acceptance (opt-in) is a condition. Receipts from training/test mode must be clearly labelled invalid (e.g. 'Test not valid').
DK.mandatoryFields: Verified (info.skat.dk): Till receipt (kassebon) replacing a simplified invoice must show company name OR registration (CVR) number, issue date, nature of the supply (may be summarised), VAT amount (may be stated as 20% of price incl. VAT); no sequential number needed. Simplified invoice (sales < DKK 3,000) shows: company name and address, CVR/SE number, sequential invoice number, date, quantity and type of goods/services, total amount and VAT amount. Under the digital sales registration regime the electronic journal also holds CVR, unique consecutive transaction number, start/end time, payment method and system serial number. Section numbering in the VAT Order (momsbekendtgorelsen par. 63/64/66) differs across sources - verify on retsinformation.dk.
DK.fiscalSystem: Verified: Denmark has NO certified fiscal device. Since 1 Jan 2024 businesses with turnover < DKK 10m in listed sectors (cafes/bars/nightclubs, pizzerias/fast food/ice cream, grocers and 24h kiosks, restaurants; judged on actual operation; SKAT can order other businesses to use one; supermarkets/webshops/door-to-door partly excluded) must use a digital salgsregistreringssystem meeting momsbekendtgorelsen par. 64: electronic journal logging all actions, transaction data digitally signed with OCES (or eIDAS) certificate, no ability to add/edit/delete, SAF-T export, X and Z reports, cash must be accepted and recorded, online/portal sales recorded, system clock changes logged. Skattestyrelsen does NOT approve/certify systems; supplier may document with ISAE 3402 declaration; responsibility lies with the merchant. No registration with the tax authority found. Fines DKK 10,000 / 20,000 / 30,000 per control visit plus daily fines of min DKK 1,000 (skat.dk).
DK.realTimeReporting: None found. Data delivered as signed SAF-T on request; no continuous reporting (verified absence in skat.dk page, not proven by a statement).
DK.receiptIdentifiers: Transaction numbers are unique and consecutive in the electronic journal; digital signature (OCES) on journal data, not printed. No QR/control code on receipts found. Receipt sequential number not required for kassebon.
DK.retentionYears: 5 years from end of the financial year the material relates to (Bogforingsloven par. 12, verified via Erhvervsstyrelsen); digital sales-registration data min 5 years from end of relevant financial year (skat.dk). Sales/purchase documents must be stored digitally in a digital bookkeeping system.

vat.reduced: None for food or hospitality (Denmark has a single 25% rate; some exemptions e.g. passenger transport, healthcare). Verified from general knowledge, not rechecked.
vat.changesToWatch: Bogforingsloven digital bookkeeping duty phased in; financial companies from 1 Jan 2026 (Erhvervsstyrelsen). Nothing receipt-specific for 2026-27 found.

other.extra: Merchants are legally required to accept cash (per Skattestyrelsen FAQ) - exact exemptions unverified.

FI.name: Finland
FI.receiptObligation: Verified (vero.fi): the seller must offer a receipt for cash and equivalent payments (cash or card, presented as 'kuitintarjoamisvelvollisuus'); buyer may always request one in a cash sale. Applies to businesses and sole traders with fiscal-year turnover > EUR 10,000 and to associations with business activity above the same threshold. Exempt: automatic vending, lottery-law activities, outdoor market/street trading (except alcohol retail/serving), non-profit/hobby activity under the threshold, farming/forestry, e-commerce and payments the buyer makes independently without the seller present. Indoor sales and outdoor alcohol serving always need a receipt. Late-payment penalty EUR 300-1,000 (vero.fi).
FI.digitalReceipt: Verified (vero.fi): the receipt can be printed, handwritten or electronic; the seller chooses the form; the customer may decline a receipt (no printing needed). No explicit consent/opt-in rule found other than GDPR.
FI.mandatoryFields: Verified (vero.fi): business name, contact details and business ID (y-tunnus); issue date; sequential identification number; quantity and type of goods / type of services; amount paid including VAT and VAT rates. If several sellers share a receipt, the selling business must be identifiable.
FI.fiscalSystem: No certified/fiscal cash register or control-unit regime found in force in Finland (a cash register is not mandatory; other devices or handwritten receipts are accepted per vero.fi). A 2018 fiscal-cash-register discussion existed (industry statements) but I found no enacted law - treat as 'none in force, unverified for 2026-27'. Cash sales must be recorded in daily order; register sales reports (or receipt copies) are attached as vouchers.
FI.realTimeReporting: None for POS sales found. Finland runs a Real-Time Economy programme (e-receipts/e-invoices; State Treasury) and a Ministry of Finance draft amends the Tax Procedure Act (digital reporting, mostly from 1 Jan 2028, comments due 2 Oct 2026) - not confirmed to cover POS receipts.
FI.receiptIdentifiers: Sequential identification number only. No QR/control code requirement found.
FI.retentionYears: Vouchers/receipts and business correspondence: min 6 years after end of the fiscal year (Kirjanpitolaki 2:10; verified via secondary sources); ledgers, financial statements 10 years. Electronic storage allowed.

other.cashRounding: Cash totals rounded to nearest 5 cents (1 and 2 cent coins not used; euro-area practice, Act on rounding) - from general knowledge, unverified in this session.

NO.name: Norway
NO.receiptObligation: Verified (Skatteetaten): bookkeeping-obligated businesses must record and document cash sales (incl. card payments settled on delivery; online sales are not cash sales) in a kassasystem with product declaration (Bokforingsloven par. 10a, since 1 Jan 2019); a sale cannot be completed without a sales receipt being produced (printed or electronically sent). Exemptions: cash sales <= NOK 50,000 excl. VAT per accounting year; mobile/occasional sales <= 3x national insurance basic amount (G); alternative: kontantfaktura with customer name/address on every sale.
NO.digitalReceipt: Verified (Skatteetaten): system must be able to print on paper, but receipt may instead be sent electronically (email, Digipost, to phone); electronic receipts must be headed 'Elektronisk salgskvittering'; if both sent and printed, one must be marked 'KOPI'; sending to an address the customer cannot receive from does not comply; customer can give email verbally (no formal consent format).
NO.mandatoryFields: Verified (Skatteetaten, kassasystemforskriften + bokforingsforskriften par. 5-3-2a/ch. 5-1): word 'Salgskvittering' at the top (Norwegian heading; 'Returkvittering' for returns); seller name, organisation number followed by 'MVA' if VAT-registered; date and time; POS/cash point ID; payment method; integrated payment terminal -> transaction ID; item description/quantity, price, VAT rate and amount, total (general sales-document content in bokforingsforskriften ch. 5-1; exact list unverified here). Copies marked 'KOPI', max one copy.
NO.fiscalSystem: Verified: Kassasystemloven + kassasystemforskriften. Cash register systems must have a product declaration (produkterklaering) submitted by the supplier via Altinn (no government approval/certificate, a supplier self-declaration), electronic journal, SAF-T Cash Register XML export, X and Z reports, return/delivery receipts. Applies to all bookkeeping-obligated businesses with cash sales above exemption. The merchant keeps the system description and electronic journal. No hardware control unit.
NO.realTimeReporting: None found. SAF-T export delivered on request/audit (verified that SAF-T exists; absence of real-time reporting is not explicitly confirmed).
NO.receiptIdentifiers: Heading 'Salgskvittering'/'Elektronisk salgskvittering'/'KOPI'; POS ID, transaction ID (integrated terminal). No QR/control-code requirement found (unverified).
NO.retentionYears: 5 years (Bokforingsloven par. 13; general rule; cash-system documentation/electronic journal also 5 years per a secondary source; electronic journal must be kept for the full period, SAF-T alone insufficient). Verify at Lovdata.

IS.name: Iceland
IS.receiptObligation: Verified (skatturinn.is): VAT-registered retailers/service providers selling mainly to final consumers may use a cash register (sjodvel) instead of sales invoices; a receipt must be given with each sale; the register/display must be visible to the customer. Business customers can request an invoice (register receipt can serve if it meets invoice content, has a sequential number and electronic-journal marking). Customers under ISK 6,000 need not have name/kennitala recorded. Exemptions: unverified.
IS.digitalReceipt: Partly verified: electronic (paperless) sales invoices allowed if all conditions are met. Whether a cash-register receipt may be delivered electronically instead of paper, and consent conditions: unverified.
IS.mandatoryFields: Verified (skatturinn.is) for sales invoices: seller name, kennitala, VAT number; date; buyer name and kennitala (exceptions for consumer cash sales/small sales); type of sale and description; quantity, unit price, total; whether VAT included; VAT amount (for consumer sales stating the VAT share suffices: 19.35% of total at 24%, 9.91% at 11%); taxable and exempt sales and rates separated; sequential numbering (pre-printed, separate sequence per VAT number; electronic invoices follow other rules). Cash register outer receipt must show the breakdown by VAT rate and date. 11% goods must be clearly marked.
IS.fiscalSystem: Verified: no certified control unit found. Regulation 50/1993 on bookkeeping and income recording sets minimum cash register requirements: outer (customer) receipt, inner strip or electronic journal, daily sales counter by rate, grand-total counter, daily Z report (settlement at least daily). Registration with the tax authority: not found. Regulatory overhaul of bookkeeping law in consultation (Aug-Sep 2026, S-151/2026; draft) - not in force.
IS.receiptIdentifiers: Sequential number (if register receipt serves as invoice), Z report counters, electronic-journal marking. No QR/control code found.
IS.retentionYears: Unverified in this session (general knowledge: 7 years under Log um bokhald nr. 145/1994). Register inner strips/electronic journals must be kept complete and unbroken like other accounting records.

EU.name: European Union baseline
EU.vatDirectiveInvoices: Directive 2006/112/EC (consolidated). Art. 220: invoice mandatory for supplies to other taxable persons/legal persons, distance sales/intra-EU supplies etc.; B2C domestic retail supplies are not required to get an invoice at EU level. Art. 226: list of mandatory fields on full invoices (date, sequential number, supplier and customer VAT ID/name/address, quantity and nature of goods/services, date of supply, taxable amount per rate, rate, VAT amount, exemption reference etc.). Art. 226b: simplified invoice content - date of issue, supplier identity, type of goods/services, VAT amount or data to calculate it, reference to original in case of credit note (reduced content list; confirm exact wording at EUR-Lex). Art. 238: Member States MAY allow simplified invoices where the amount does not exceed EUR 100 (or equivalent), or for credit notes, or where commercial/administrative practice makes full invoice difficult; Art. 238(1) cap from memory, verify. Art. 232-233: e-invoices subject to recipient acceptance and authenticity/integrity guarantees (modified by ViDA).
EU.receiptsHarmonised: Consumer POS receipts are NOT EU-harmonised: whether and what receipt must be issued is national (confirmed pattern across SE/DK/FI/NO/IS above). EU level only defines invoices/simplified invoices (VAT Directive). No EU-wide fiscal register or e-receipt standard exists.
EU.vida: Directive (EU) 2025/516 (ViDA) adopted 11 Mar 2025, OJ 25 Mar 2025, in force 14 Apr 2025 (secondary source lookuptax). Key dates: from 14 Apr 2025 Member States may mandate domestic e-invoicing without a derogation; from 1 Jul 2030 mandatory structured e-invoicing (EN 16931) and digital reporting for intra-EU B2B supplies; 2035 further alignment for Member States with existing national DRR systems. B2C is outside the mandatory EU regime (Member States may optionally extend digital reporting to domestic B2C) - not directly affecting retail receipts. Norway/Iceland (EEA, not EU VAT) are not bound by ViDA; Nordic EU states (SE, DK, FI) are.
EU.euLevelEReceiptDiscussions: No Commission legislative proposal for mandatory or optional e-receipts found in this session; only national measures (France no automatic paper receipts since 2023, Belgium optional paper, Austria digital receipts from Oct 2026, Germany draft law digital receipts default from 2028 - news/blog sources, not verified against official texts; Finland Real-Time Economy / eKuitti). EU-level work is limited to e-invoicing standards (EN 16931, Peppol). Treat 'EU e-receipt initiative' as unverified.
EU.gdpr: Regulation (EU) 2016/679, applicable also in Norway and Iceland via EEA. Points: data minimisation and purpose limitation (Art. 5(1)(b),(c)) - do not require name/email for basic receipt unless legally needed; storage limitation (Art. 5(1)(e)); retention of accounting records is a legal obligation (Art. 6(1)(c)) and justifies refusing erasure of the fiscal part (Art. 17(3)(b)) while personal identifiers (email, wallet link) can be erased/pseudonymised once not needed; transparency (Art. 13); marketing via receipt email/app needs separate consent under ePrivacy rules (Directive 2002/58/EC Art. 13) - receipts must not be bundled with marketing consent; wallet apps that link purchase history are profiling risk (DPIA likely). Confirm with DPO.
EU.eaa: European Accessibility Act, Directive (EU) 2019/882: applies from 28 Jun 2025 to e-commerce services, consumer banking, e-books, consumer-facing terminals etc.; micro-enterprises (<10 staff and <=EUR 2m turnover) providing services are exempt (Art. 4(5)). A buyer-facing receipts/wallet app is likely in scope when part of an e-commerce service or offered by a non-micro provider; self-service payment terminals are in scope. National transposition: SE, DK, FI, NO, IS laws not individually verified. Seek legal assessment of applicability to the platform and to merchants' receipt screens. Practical: WCAG 2.1 AA (EN 301 549) for the wallet app and email/web receipts.
